annotations.title: Put new screenshots in a set

description: Use this when a set needs new screenshots in its phones: a recapture, a fixed screen, or a phone frame layer to fill (get_asset shows those as "phone frame: ..."), in a set the user saved (asset_id) or a set or design you made in this conversation (handle). Two calls. First with asset_id or handle and screens (each a screen number, the local file and, for a phone frame layer, its id): it returns one upload command (bash and PowerShell) that sends the files straight to storage. Run it, then call again with the same asset_id or handle, replace_handle and the revision get_asset returned: the files are checked (PNG or JPEG, the shape of the phone's screen) and swapped in, and the reply has the new revision and previews. With asset_id (something the user saved) it needs the user signed in to appdesigns (in Claude Code type /mcp, pick appdesigns and choose Authenticate (or run `claude mcp login appdesigns` in a separate terminal), in Codex run `codex mcp login appdesigns`; other agents open the sign-in page themselves); with handle (a set or design you made in this conversation, not saved yet) it needs no sign-in.

handle.description: Instead of asset_id: the project_handle create_project returned or the design_handle create_design returned, for something you made in this conversation that the user has not saved yet. Needs no sign-in.

replace_handle.description: Second call: the replace_handle the first call returned, once the upload command has run.

revision.description: Second call: the revision get_asset (or the last edit) returned.

screens.description: First call: what goes where, at most 6 files a call.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the PNG or JPEG (no ~ or $VARIABLES). Not read by the server; it goes into the upload command.

layer.description: A phone frame layer's id from get_asset; leave it out for the screen's own phone.

name: replace_screenshots
title: Put new screenshots in a set
